summary: Telemetry bar-indicator particle renderer. When the scoring gate dword_8AB6E4 equals 2 it delegates via Delegation(&dword_8AB6EC), otherwise it falls back to the session-time global dbl_8AFEA0 as the reference time. Iterates the particle array at this+0x68 (count at this+0x64), computing two fade values per particle from its lifetime fields (particle+8 start, particle+12 end, particle+96/particle+100 fade thresholds) scaled by this+0x40. Particles whose reference time falls inside the lifetime window with any non-zero fade are drawn by writing four pixel attributes to the particle's texture; particles outside the window are removed from the array via ArrayElementRemoval.

operations.description: If dword_8AB6E4 == 2, call Delegation(&dword_8AB6EC) to obtain the reference data; otherwise use dbl_8AFEA0 as the reference time.
Read the particle count from this+0x64 and the particle array pointer from this+0x68; prepare the loop counter.
Iterate each particle block: v4 = array entry at this+0x68 + 4*index; continue while the index is below the count at this+0x64.
Compute normalized lifetime progress v8 = (reference time - particle start field) * scale factor from this+0x40.

Fade A: when v8 is below the particle's first fade threshold, compute the fade attribute as (threshold - v8) * 254 packed into a 24-bit color (shifted left by 24 plus 0xFFFFFF); otherwise keep it zero.
Fade B: when v8 is below the particle's second fade threshold, compute the second fade attribute similarly from (threshold - v8) * 254; otherwise keep it zero.
If the reference time is inside the particle's lifetime window (>= start and <= end) and either fade attribute is non-zero, render the particle.
PixelAttributeWriteToTexture(texture, 0, fadeA), (texture, 1, fadeB), (texture, 2, fadeB), (texture, 3, fadeA): write four pixel attributes to the particle's texture using the two computed fades.
ArrayElementRemoval(this, v4): remove the particle from the array when it falls outside the lifetime window or both fades are zero; rewind the index so the shifted element is re-examined.
Return the final loop index (last value of the counter).

unresolved: flt_5ACEC4 is listed as a global in the packet but is not read anywhere in this function's raw source; it appears only in the existing_analysis fill, so it is recorded here.
The per-particle fields p[2], p[3], p[24], p[25] have no packet field evidence entries; their dword indices come only from the raw source.
The exact pixel-attribute semantics (color vs. alpha/fade channel) of the four PixelAttributeWriteToTexture writes are inferred from the call name and the two computed fades.
